newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent dives as U.S. mogas collapses, funds exit.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent dives as U.S. mogas collapses, funds exit.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures slumped late on Wednesday, ending over $1 a barrel off session highs as collapsing U.S. gasoline prices and investment fund selling undermined the market, brokers said.
"There's not been much in terms of news but we have seen some fund selling coming into the States," said a broker.
Others said sharp losses on the expiring Dec WTI NYMEX crude contract added to the slide, which triggered stop-loss selling as Jan Brent broke technical support levels.
"It smashed through several including Monday's low of $22.85 and $22.75 which was the low on November 12," said a broker.
Jan Brent settled 84 cents down at $22.50 a barrel after touching a high of $23.70 earlier in the day.
Light early afternoon profit-taking heralded worse to come as NYMEX gasoline started to plummet despite reports of falling crude and product stocks in the U.S, dealers said.

But even though gasoline stocks were down last week, American Petroleum Institute data showed output increased to 7.78 million gallons a day from 7.43 million the previous week as a number of catalytic crackers came back on line, they said.
"(U.S.) gasoline went first as the market attempted to break through recent highs and failed," said a broker.
Strong equity and bond markets in the U.S. may also have drawn some fund money out of oil futures, he added.
"Equities and bonds are looking better because inflation prospects are better so some of the hedge funds may have decided they no longer need to hold raw materials," said one.

Earlier, Dec gas oil ended mid-range but still $2.00 higher at $223.50 a tonne with most attention again focussed on the delivery of 865,100 tonnes against the expired Nov contract. Cargill Investor Services said it was working with the IPE, on behalf of Cargill International -- the main Nov long -- to enure an orderly delivery.--Mark Thompson, +44 171 542 7930
